title: Quasi-isomorphism of flat ringed Cech base-change data
statement: Let phi:R -> B be a map of commutative ring sheaves on a small site, and I an ideal subsheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-ideal] with locally finite-type underlying module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Suppose the restricted B-module is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and I.IsQuotientIso phi. Let epsilon:K -> R[0] be an unbounded module complex [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] having the augmented local extended Cech description [def-weil-pbc-local-extended-cech-description], with the source and source-slice derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] assumed to exist. Then the unit on K of the specified termwise scalar-extension adjunction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-scalar-extension-complex-adjunction] is a quasi-isomorphism. Restriction of scalars is as in [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. This concerns the canonical scalar-extension map, not arbitrary augmentation-compatible maps.

source.place: Tags 099I and 099H, local comparison and local-to-global conclusion

proof.text: Choose local finite generating sections of I from its finite-type presentation, index each finite family by Fin r, and use the local description to obtain the derived Cech isomorphism on every generating slice.
Apply the scalar-extension-unit comparison on each finite generating slice.

Exact restriction identifies the homology maps with restrictions of the global homology map. The slices cover the site; Mathlib Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop and reflection through the underlying additive sheaf show that every global homology map is invertible.

lean.statement:
theorem flat_ringedCech_baseChange_data_quasiIso
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {R B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ B) (I : RingedSiteIdeal R)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (siteModuleRings R))]
    [∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (siteModuleRings (R.over U)))]
    (hI : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType.{u, u, u} I.module)
    (hflat : SheafOfModules.IsFlat
      ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (siteModuleRings B))))
    (hquot : I.IsQuotientIso φ)
    (K : ringedSiteComplex R) (ε : K ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex R)
    (hK : HasLocalExtendedCechDescription R I.module I.inclusion K ε) :
    QuasiIso ((ringedScalarExtensionComplexAdjunction φ).unit.app K)

statement_change.old_statement: Under the hypotheses of lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-cech-base-change, any scalar-extended augmented model (L,delta,u) satisfying the augmentation equation has u a quasi-isomorphism.
statement_change.what: The old universal statement is false: for phi=id, I=0 and K=R[0], the inclusion K -> K direct-sum K followed by first projection obeys the augmentation equation but is not a quasi-isomorphism when R is nonzero. Tag 099I specifies K prime = K tensor_R B. Replace the arbitrary augmented map by the canonical termwise scalar-extension unit, and adapt the sole consumer without changing its statement.

citers.note: Use actual scalar extension of K and the adjoint of epsilon followed by the coefficient map for its augmentation. The existential conclusion and every binder remain unchanged.

old_proof.text: Restrict to finite generating slices, identify the scalar-extended local terms with the extended localization complexes, apply the flat Cech comparison, and globalize the local vanishing of the kernel and cokernel of u.
